metadata.title: Analyze and Plan Fixes
metadata.purposeAndUsage: Analyze each active PR comment, read the affected code, categorize comments (Valid/Partial/Disagree), and generate a detailed fix plan document for approval. This step has an approval gate — the plan must be approved before fixes are implemented.

output.description: Fix plan document with categorized comments and proposed fixes

prerequisites: activeThreads array available in memory from fetch-pr-comments step
activeThreadCount > 0 (if 0, this step should not run — template handles early exit)
Local workspace checked out to the PR branch
specificActions: Follow the substeps below in sequence
Workflow: extract comment metadata → read affected code → categorize comments → generate fix plan → present for approval
Be objective when categorizing — provide technical justification for Disagree, not opinions
Include enough code context to understand the issue without reading the entire file
Each proposed fix should be copy-paste ready when possible
Use mermaid diagrams when the fix involves multiple components, control flow, or dependency relationships

read: Local source code files referenced by comments

tools: Read - Read local source code files at commented lines
bestPractices: Read +/-10 lines of context around the commented line range for better understanding
When categorizing as Disagree, always provide a technical justification with references (docs, patterns, framework constraints)
Group comments by file when generating the plan for easier review
Include the full comment conversation context — reviewers may have clarified their intent in follow-up messages
For Partial comments, clearly state what can be done now vs what needs discussion

valid.label: To Fix
valid.criteria: Comment identifies a genuine issue that should be fixed

partial.label: Need Discussion
partial.criteria: Comment has merit but the fix is unclear or needs design discussion

disagree.label: Disagree
disagree.criteria: Comment is incorrect or the current approach is better

substeps.name: Extract Comment Metadata
substeps.description: Parse each active thread into structured analysis input
actions: Read activeThreads from memory
For each thread extract: threadId, filePath, lineRange (start-end), comment text (first comment content), author, full conversation (all replies)
Build a list of unique files referenced by comments
Log: 'Analyzing {count} comments across {fileCount} files'

substeps.name: Read Affected Code
substeps.description: Read the local source code at each commented location
actions: For each unique file referenced by comments:
- Read the file from the local workspace
- For each comment on this file: extract the line range with +/-10 lines of surrounding context
- If the file doesn't exist locally: log warning 'File not in workspace: {path}' — may need to check out the PR branch
Log: 'Read {count} files, {warnings} warnings'

substeps.name: Categorize Comments
substeps.description: Assess each comment and assign a category
actions: For each comment, considering the code context and conversation:
- Valid: The comment identifies a genuine issue. Determine the specific fix.
- Partial: The comment has merit but the resolution needs discussion. Identify what can be done now vs what needs alignment.
- Disagree: The current code is correct or the suggestion would cause issues. Prepare technical justification.
Record the category, reasoning, and proposed action for each comment
Tally quick stats: count per category

substeps.name: Generate Fix Plan Document
substeps.description: Create the fix plan markdown document
actions: Create fix-plan.md in the process directory with:
Header: PR number, title, active comment count, repository name
Quick Stats: count per category (To Fix / Need Discussion / Disagree)
Per-comment section with:
- Thread ID and brief summary
- Reviewer name, file path, line range
- Full quoted comment text
- Current code snippet (fenced block)
- Assessment with category indicator
- For Valid: proposed fix as code block + explanation
- For Partial: proposed approach + discussion points
- For Disagree: justification bullets + suggested reply text
- Mermaid diagram when the fix involves component interactions, control flow, or state changes
Log: 'Generated fix-plan.md with {total} comments ({valid} to fix, {partial} to discuss, {disagree} disagreed)'

substeps.name: Store Results in Memory
substeps.description: Record the fix plan details for downstream steps
actions: Write to memory: fixPlan.stats (counts by category), fixPlan.comments (array of categorized comment objects), fixPlan.artifactPath (path to fix-plan.md)
Each comment object includes: threadId, filePath, lineRange, category, proposedAction, replyText

substeps.name: End-Step: Compliance Check
substeps.description: Verify principles were followed in this step
actions: Verify: Was log.json updated for any user interactions?
Verify: Were mandatory actions confirmed with output?
Verify: fix-plan.md was created with all categorized comments
Verify: All comments were categorized (no uncategorized)
Output: 'Step completed in compliance with operating principles'

flow.description: Linear flow: Extract comment metadata → Read affected code files → Categorize each comment → Generate fix-plan.md → Store in memory → Compliance check. This step has approvalRequired: true in the template — the fix plan is presented to the user for approval before implementation.

memoryFileUsage.readFrom: activeThreads, pr.title, repository.name from previous steps
fields: Information Produced: fixPlan.stats (valid/partial/disagree counts), fixPlan.comments (array with threadId, filePath, lineRange, category, proposedAction, replyText per comment), fixPlan.artifactPath
Decisions Made: Category assignment per comment with reasoning
Notes: Files not found locally, comments with ambiguous categorization

requiredFiles: Local source code files referenced by PR comments
